te: Meeting summary video · Starting a study on the Learning Promotion Act, and approving the report on children without Thai nationality
Draft report on checking the personal status of cross-border students in schools
se: The meeting considered the draft study report on oversight and checking of the personal status of cross-border students in schools, with Trat, Chanthaburi and Sa Kaeo as case studies. The draft says Thailand has rules that guarantee the right to education of people without civil registration documents or Thai nationality, but border areas still face challenges with documents, several data systems and the transfer of data. The G-Code is a tool to identify learners, not proof of nationality, so it should not be a condition that makes children wait to enrol. The draft proposes work in 3 phases (within 6 months, 6–18 months and 18–36 months), such as data and G-Code service standards, enrolling children before their documents are complete, and a complaints channel. The meeting noted the draft and asked its authors to revise it in line with the meeting's observations before it is presented again.
it: Draft study report: oversight and checking of the personal status of cross-border students in schools (Trat, Chanthaburi and Sa Kaeo)
Proposed work in 3 phases: data and G-Code service standards, enrolment before documents are complete, and a complaints channel

te: Meeting summary video · Draft report on checking the personal status of cross-border students in schools
A framework of policy proposals in 4 areas for fiscal year 2027, and 4 finished reports
se: The meeting considered ways to drive policy mechanisms to improve learning promotion, private education, special education and educational equality, and set its work framework for fiscal year 2027. It noted 4 finished study reports ready to go to the committee: education for children without Thai nationality and children of migrant workers (Myanmar); education for qualifications for cross-border children; personnel management of teachers under the Department of Learning Encouragement in remote highland areas of the North; and personnel management of teachers at special education centres. It set proposal themes in 4 areas: a credit bank system backed by law, per-head subsidies for private schools that match real costs, solving the shortage of special education teachers, and a mechanism to bring out-of-school children back into education. The meeting agreed to a field visit in Chiang Mai to study the use of technology to screen the development of children with disabilities aged 0–5 in remote areas.
it: 4 finished study reports, ready to go to the committee
Framework of policy proposal themes in 4 areas for fiscal year 2027
Field visit to Chiang Mai: technology for early screening of the development of children with disabilities in remote areas

te: Meeting summary video · A framework of policy proposals in 4 areas for fiscal year 2027, and 4 finished reports
Raising standards of non-formal private schools, seminar results, and a study plan on the Student Loan Fund
se: The meeting considered 3 matters. First, progress of the working group on policy proposals to strengthen standards in private education, which is drafting a report on promoting, supporting and raising the standards of non-formal private schools. The meeting discussed the definitions, title and scope of the study, focusing on why some providers of teaching have not entered the licensing system, and proposed grouping them by risk; the working group was asked to improve the content. Second, the results of a public hearing seminar on 9 September 2026, with proposals in 4 areas: learning promotion, private education, special education and educational equality. The 4 working groups were asked to build these into the next stage of study. Third, the plan of the working group on solving student loan problems with the Student Loan Fund, which will answer a set of questions in 11 areas by the end of October. The meeting agreed to wait for this information before drafting policy proposals and then inviting the agencies concerned to discuss them.
it: Progress on the draft report: promoting, supporting and raising the standards of non-formal private schools
Results of the public hearing seminar of 9 September 2026: proposals in 4 areas
Study plan on solving student loan problems, with the Student Loan Fund
